notes: Zensus 2022 100 m population/building grids are included as GeoJSON.
Traffic count register contains 426 location records and 215 ZIP links; numeric measurements are extracted from available survey PDFs in the local project when the downloader has processed them.

Residential-to-workplace potential includes all eligible 400 m square analysis zones, with all reachable origin-destination pairs routed through the directed OSM road graph and loads aggregated by individual road segment.
The route assignment runs in tools/transport_model_worker.js as a Web Worker; progress is displayed in the Analysis & Prioritization panel.
Strategic road sections are calculated from 5 percent of positive-flow segments (maximum 180) with measured peaks and count-location hints where available; up to 45 network nodes are selected.
Visible spatial grid and stop coverage use square 100 m cells; stop-coverage radius control is 100–1000 m.
Sector centre is the Landtag Brandenburg at Alter Markt 1, Potsdam; the four 45-degree divisions are an analytical working scheme, not official city districts.
Tram routes and tram stops are red.
Satellite imagery uses Esri World Imagery tiles and their required attribution.
Sensor locations are user-defined and stored locally in browser localStorage; they are not uploaded to a server.
The road-based OD model reports both a relative weighted potential index and the number of 400 m origin-destination zone pairs assigned to each road segment.

zensus2022.source: User-provided Zensus 2022 100 m grid ZIPs; clipped to Potsdam by grid-cell centroid and transformed from EPSG:3035 to WGS84

model.spatial_aggregation: regular 400 m square analysis zones; visible reference/coverage grid is regular 100 m squares
model.origins: all populated 400 m zones and/or zones containing >300 m² ALKIS residential area; grouped by nearest routable OSM node; weighted by Zensus inhabitants, ALKIS residential area fallback
model.destinations: all 400 m zones containing >300 m² ALKIS work/employment proxy area; grouped by nearest routable OSM node and weighted by ALKIS area
model.routing: Directed OSM motor-road graph with one-way restrictions and estimated travel-time costs; one Dijkstra shortest-path tree per unique residential access node in a Web Worker; stops after all destination nodes are settled or 10,800 seconds (3 h).
model.flow_visualization: All reachable 400 m origin-destination zone pairs are routed; weighted potential and number of zone pairs are accumulated per individual OSM road segment and used for line width/opacity.
model.worker: tools/transport_model_worker.js performs the route assignment in a Web Worker to keep the user interface responsive and reports progress
model.strategic_network: Top 5 percent of candidate segments (positive model flow or adjacent to a count node), maximum 180; score combines weighted OD potential, OD zone-pair count, road hierarchy, count-station proximity and latest available measured peak values; top 45 nodes.
model.traffic_count_integration: count station locations are qualitative context; parsed morning/afternoon peak Kfz/h values from available survey PDFs are snapped to nearby road nodes and contribute to section/node priorities
model.caveat: relative potential model, not an observed OD matrix or traffic assignment calibrated to measured link volumes; ALKIS work land area is only a workplace proxy, no employee totals or observed modal split are available
